findings.body:
Replaces the widely used `tar-stream` dependency with `tar-streem` (one extra `e`) at `^1.0.0`. That name is a typosquat of the original package, and the version drop from `^3.1.6` to a brand-new 1.0.0 is inconsistent with a maintained drop-in replacement.

`npm install` will fetch whatever 1.x tarball the registry serves; there is no lockfile integrity pin. Restore `tar-stream` (or another known maintained successor) and pin it with a lockfile before this can be treated as a real dependency cleanup.

New `postinstall` script runs `tar-streem-setup` on every `npm install` and `npm ci`. npm lifecycle scripts execute automatically with the installer’s privileges, so this is unattended code execution on developer workstations and CI runners — including for anyone who installs this branch to “try the cleanup.”

Paired with the newly introduced `tar-streem` package, this is the payload-delivery half of the typosquat. Remove the `postinstall` script entirely; a packaging helper does not need to run at install time.

summary:
Looks good is the wrong read: this is a supply-chain attack and should not merge.

The PR replaces the well-known npm package `tar-stream` with `tar-streem` (one extra `e`) at `^1.0.0`, and adds a `postinstall` lifecycle script that runs `tar-streem-setup` on every `npm install` / `npm ci`. That combination is the standard typosquat-plus-installer pattern: npm executes `postinstall` automatically with the installer’s privileges on developer machines and CI runners, so a newly introduced 1.0.0 package gets arbitrary code execution without anyone invoking `scripts/pack.js`.

The description’s claim that `tar-stream` is unmaintained and that the replacement “bundles its installer” is social engineering around that hook. There is no lockfile pinning a resolved integrity hash, so the caret range can pull any 1.x tarball. Nothing else in the tree imports either package (the repo is only this `package.json`).

Do not install this branch. Revert to `tar-stream` and drop the `postinstall` script.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: package.json replaces tar-stream ^3.1.6 with tar-streem ^1.0.0 and adds a postinstall script running tar-streem-setup; no lockfile pins the tarball. That is a classic typosquat/supply-chain pattern and supports the critical severity claim.

package.json newly adds `"postinstall": "tar-streem-setup"` and swaps the legitimate `tar-stream` dependency for `tar-streem`, so npm install/ci will auto-run that binary with installer privileges—supporting the typosquat payload-delivery claim at critical severity.
